notes.made: Temperton wrote and arranged it, the slow closer of Thriller, cut at Westlake with Louis Johnson on bass, Jeff Porcaro on drums, Paul Jackson Jr. on guitar, Greg Phillinganes on Rhodes, David Paich and Steve Porcaro on synths and Michael Boddicker on Emulator. In his memoir Moonwalk, Jackson wrote that Jones still wasn't happy after dozens of takes and told him to beg, so he had the lights turned off and the curtain closed and sang it again; that take is the record. An extra verse and chorus were cut, and the longer version surfaced on a 2002 Temperton compilation.
notes.context: It closes the album, and J. Randy Taraborrelli called it the closest Jackson had come to crooning a sexy, soulful ballad since his Motown years. It was the only one of the nine songs never issued as a single in any form, and Jackson never sang it live. Its second life came through hip-hop and R&B producers, who kept sampling it, usually pitched up.

culture.title: Hey Lover
culture.line: LL Cool J and Boyz II Men's 1995 single samples it and reached number 3 on the Hot 100; Angie Stone's Lover's Ghetto and Chris Brown's Transparency use it too.

culture.title: Benson's guitar
culture.line: George Benson's instrumental from Guitar Man (2011) spent two weeks at number one on Billboard's Smooth Jazz Airplay chart in February 2012.

culture.title: Maxwell, 2022
culture.line: Jackson never sang it live; Maxwell did, at the 2022 Billboard Music Awards to open the Thriller 40 celebrations.
